data.title: B2 Level Check
data.description: A mixed grammar and usage check to estimate whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B2 level.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using the third conditional.
sections.explain: Use 'if' + past perfect and 'would have' + past participle to describe an unreal past situation.

words.word: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended.
If I knew about the meeting, I would have attended.
If I had known about the meeting, I would attend.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct mixed conditional sentence.
sections.explain: A past condition can have a present result. Use past perfect in the if-clause and 'would' + base verb for the present result.

words.word: If I had taken that job, I would be living in London now.
If I took that job, I would have been living in London now.
If I had taken that job, I would have lived in London now.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct passive reporting structure.
sections.explain: Formal English often uses 'is believed to' or similar passive reporting structures.

words.word: The company is believed to be considering a merger.
The company is believed that it is considering a merger.
The company believes to be considering a merger.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct past modal for deduction.
sections.explain: Use 'must have' + past participle for a strong deduction about a past event.

words.word: She must have forgotten about the appointment.
She must forgot about the appointment.
She must have forget about the appointment.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using inversion.
sections.explain: After a negative adverbial such as 'rarely' at the beginning of a sentence, use auxiliary-verb inversion.

words.word: Rarely have I seen such an impressive performance.
Rarely I have seen such an impressive performance.
Rarely have seen I such an impressive performance.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct reduced relative clause.
sections.explain: A passive relative clause can often be reduced by removing the relative pronoun and the verb 'be'.

words.word: The documents submitted yesterday are being reviewed.
The documents were submitted yesterday are being reviewed.
The documents submitting yesterday are being reviewed.

sections.explain: 'Despite' is followed by a noun, pronoun or -ing form, not a full clause beginning directly with subject and verb.

words.word: Despite feeling tired, she continued working.
Despite she felt tired, she continued working.
Despite of feeling tired, she continued working.

sections.explain: Use 'wish' + past perfect to express regret about a past situation.

words.word: I wish I had listened to your advice.
I wish I listened to your advice.
I wish I would have listened to your advice.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct future perfect sentence.
sections.explain: Use 'will have' + past participle for something expected to be completed before a future point.

words.word: By next June, I will have worked here for ten years.
By next June, I will work here for ten years.
By next June, I will have work here for ten years.

sections.explain: A cleft sentence such as 'What I need is...' is used to emphasise a particular part of the message.

words.word: What I need most is a few days off.
What I need most are to have a few days off.
That I need most is a few days off.
